models.author: Aryuemaan Chowdhury
models.description:
# Model Summary

Wiola is an experimental, decoder-only Small Language Model (SLM) architecture built entirely from first principles and implemented in PyTorch. The architecture introduces five novel neural network components designed to improve positional representation, information flow across transformer layers, computational efficiency during training, feed-forward expressiveness, and normalization stability.

Unlike many existing language models that modify only one aspect of the transformer architecture, Wiola simultaneously proposes innovations in positional encoding, attention, feed-forward networks, normalization, and training efficiency.

The architecture is fully compatible with the Hugging Face Transformers ecosystem through `trust_remote_code=True` and currently supports four model configurations:

| Model | Parameters |
|--------|-----------:|
| Wiola-120M | ~120 Million |
| Wiola-360M | ~360 Million |
| Wiola-700M | ~700 Million |
| Wiola-1.5B | ~1.5 Billion |

The model uses:

- Decoder-only transformer architecture
- 32,000-token byte-level BPE vocabulary
- 2,048-token context window
- PyTorch implementation
- Hugging Face integration
- Autoregressive causal language modeling objective

The five novel architectural components are:

- **SRPE (Spiral Rotary Positional Encoding)**
- **GCLA (Gated Cross-Layer Attention)**
- **ATM (Adaptive Token Merging)**
- **DSFF (Dual-Stream Feed Forward)**
- **WiolaRMSNorm**

At the time of publication, the repository provides the complete architecture, training framework, tokenizer pipeline, evaluation scripts, and documentation. Pretrained checkpoints and benchmark evaluations will be released after large-scale training.

---

# Usage

Wiola can be used for:

- Text generation
- Instruction tuning
- Continued pretraining
- Research on efficient language model architectures
- Fine-tuning for downstream NLP tasks

## Loading the Model

```python
from transformers import AutoTokenizer, AutoModelForCausalLM

repo = "oscowlai/wiola-120m"

tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(
    repo,
    trust_remote_code=True
)

model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(
    repo,
    trust_remote_code=True
)
```

## Text Generation

```python
inputs = tokenizer(
    "Artificial Intelligence will",
    return_tensors="pt"
)

outputs = model.generate(
    **inputs,
    max_new_tokens=64
)

print(tokenizer.decode(outputs[0], skip_special_tokens=True))
```

## Input

- UTF-8 text
- Automatically tokenized into byte-level BPE tokens
- Maximum context length: 2,048 tokens

Input tensor shape:

```
(batch_size, sequence_length)
```

## Output

The model produces logits over the vocabulary for each token.

Output tensor shape:

```
(batch_size, sequence_length, vocab_size)
```

where

```
vocab_size = 32,000
```

### Known limitations

Current limitations include:

- No pretrained checkpoints released yet
- ATM operates only during training
- Long-context performance beyond 2,048 tokens has not yet been experimentally validated
- Performance metrics are unavailable until large-scale training is completed

---

# System

Wiola is a standalone decoder-only language model.

Typical inference pipeline:

```
Raw Text
      ↓
Tokenizer
      ↓
Input IDs
      ↓
Wiola Model
      ↓
Vocabulary Logits
      ↓
Generated Tokens
      ↓
Decoded Text
```

### Input Requirements

- UTF-8 text
- Hugging Face tokenizer
- PyTorch tensors

### Downstream Applications

Model outputs can be used for:

- Chatbots
- Question answering
- Summarization
- Code generation
- Retrieval-augmented generation
- Instruction following
- Research experiments

---

# Implementation Requirements

## Software

- Python 3.9+
- PyTorch
- Hugging Face Transformers
- CUDA (optional)
- Tokenizers
- Accelerate

## Hardware

The architecture supports training on:

- Single GPU
- Multi-GPU
- Distributed Data Parallel (DDP)

Recommended hardware:

| Model | Recommended GPU |
|--------|----------------|
|120M|12–16 GB VRAM|
|360M|24 GB VRAM|
|700M|40–48 GB VRAM|
|1.5B|80 GB VRAM or multi-GPU|

Inference can be performed on CPU for smaller variants, although GPU inference is recommended.

### Training Compute

The architecture supports mixed precision (FP16/BF16), checkpointing, and distributed training.

As pretrained models have not yet been released, total training FLOPs, wall-clock training time, energy consumption, and carbon footprint are currently unavailable.

---

# Model Characteristics

## Model Initialization

Wiola is designed to be trained **entirely from scratch**.

It is **not** fine-tuned from any existing language model.

All weights are randomly initialized before training.

---

## Model Stats

Current supported configurations:

| Variant | Parameters | Layers | Hidden Size |
|----------|-----------:|-------:|------------:|
|120M|~120M|12|768|
|360M|~360M|16|1024|
|700M|~700M|24|1536|
|1.5B|~1.5B|28|2048|

Additional characteristics:

- Decoder-only transformer
- Context length: 2,048 tokens
- Vocabulary: 32,000
- Grouped Query Attention
- Byte-level BPE tokenizer

Latency depends on hardware and batch size and has not yet been benchmarked.

---

## Other Details

Current implementation:

- No pruning
- No quantization
- No knowledge distillation
- No differential privacy mechanisms

Future releases may include:

- INT8 inference
- FP8 inference
- Quantized checkpoints
- Distilled variants

---

# Data Overview

The repository currently provides the complete training pipeline but does not distribute pretrained models.

---

## Training Data

The training pipeline supports either:

- Local text corpora
- Hugging Face datasets

Supported preprocessing:

- Text cleaning
- Tokenizer training
- Tokenization
- Sequence packing
- Dynamic batching

The architecture is dataset-agnostic and is compatible with multilingual or monolingual corpora.

---

## Demographic Groups

No demographic-specific datasets are included with the repository.

Dataset composition depends entirely on the corpus selected by the user during training.

Users are responsible for ensuring appropriate representation and mitigating demographic bias within their chosen datasets.

---

## Evaluation Data

The repository supports configurable train, validation, and test splits.

Typical configuration:

- Training: 98%
- Validation: 1%
- Test: 1%

No official benchmark datasets have yet been released with pretrained checkpoints.

---

# Evaluation Results

## Summary

The repository includes evaluation scripts compatible with standard language modeling benchmarks such as:

- HellaSwag
- PIQA
- ARC-Easy
- Perplexity evaluation

Since pretrained checkpoints are not yet available, benchmark results will be published in future releases.

---

## Subgroup Evaluation Results

No subgroup evaluation has been performed.

Such analyses will depend on the datasets used for model training and downstream evaluation.

---

## Fairness

No formal fairness evaluation has yet been conducted.

Future evaluations are expected to include analyses across demographic groups, languages, and task domains using established fairness metrics.

---

## Usage Limitations

Wiola is an experimental research architecture.

It should not currently be deployed in high-risk or safety-critical applications, including:

- Medical diagnosis
- Legal decision making
- Financial advice
- Autonomous systems
- Safety-critical infrastructure

Outputs should always be reviewed by humans before deployment.

Model performance depends heavily on the quality, diversity, and scale of the training data.

---

## Ethics

Wiola has been developed as an open research project intended to advance language model architecture research.

Potential risks include:

- Generation of inaccurate or misleading information
- Propagation of biases present in training data
- Hallucinated responses
- Misuse for harmful content generation

Mitigation strategies include:

- Open-source implementation for transparency
- Reproducible training pipeline
- Public documentation
- Human oversight during deployment
- Future bias and robustness evaluations before production releases

The authors encourage responsible use of the model and recommend comprehensive downstream evaluation before deployment in real-world applications.

models.description:
# Model Summary

AFNO V4 is a 16-hour PM2.5 forecasting model for the ANRF AISEHack Phase 2 Theme 2 competition (IIT Delhi), operating on a 140x124 grid at ~25 km resolution, hourly. It takes 10 hours of gridded inputs and forecasts the next 16 hours. ~7M parameters.

# Model Architecture

Input tensor: (batch, 20 channels, 10 time steps, 140, 124).

1. Per-frame 2D UNet encoder: ConvBlock 20->64 -> MaxPool -> ConvBlock 64->128 -> MaxPool -> ConvBlock 128->256 (residual conv blocks, GroupNorm, GELU).
2. Multiscale AFNO (AdaptFNO-style): 1 AFNO spectral block at the 35x31 encoder scale, then AvgPool to an 18x16 bottleneck.
3. Bottleneck AFNO: 6 AFNO blocks at 18x16, 8 blocks/heads each, MLP ratio 2.0 - global spectral token mixing via 2D FFT.
4. SimVP temporal translator (Incep1D, 4 layers): maps 10 input frames to 16 forecast frames at the bottleneck.
5. Lead-time conditioning: an Embedding(16, 256) adds a per-forecast-hour bias.
6. Post-translator AFNO: 2 AFNO blocks (the translator is pointwise in space, so these restore spatial spectral mixing).
7. UNet decoder: ConvTranspose upsampling 256->128->64->32 with last+mean skip fusion (fuse0/1/2) from the encoder.
8. Output head: Conv 32->32 -> Conv 32->1, zero-initialized.
9. Persistence residual: the network predicts a delta added to the last observed frame (output = last_log + delta), so it learns the change rather than the absolute field.

Input channels (20): observed (9) - PM2.5, q2, t2, u10, v10, pblh, psfc, swdown, rain; engineered (5) - wind speed, ventilation coefficient (PBLH x wind speed), advection tendency, PM tendency, diurnal climatology anomaly; time (2) - hour sin, hour cos; static (4) - lat, lon, PM2.5 climatology, episode sigma.

# Model Characteristics

- Horizon-weighted loss (0.7 -> 1.3 over h+1..h+16), EMA weights, 2-seed ensemble (42, 1337), per-horizon multiplicative calibration on a leak-free holdout.
- Training: leak-free temporal validation (contiguous tail block per month with a 12h gap), official STL episode masks (period=24, robust; residual > 3 sigma), hour-of-day estimation from swdown/t2 templates.

# Data Overview

WRF-Chem simulation, hourly. Trained on 4 months of 2016 (April, July, October, December); evaluated on unseen months of 2017. Index 0 = 00:00 UTC.

# Evaluation Results

Competition metric = w1*NormGlobalSMAPE + w2*NormEpisodeCorr + w3*NormEpisodeSMAPE (weights undisclosed).

- Private: 0.8833 (public 0.8959). Would rank 2nd on the final private leaderboard (1st place 0.8893).
- Prior v3 baseline: private 0.8609. Persistence baseline NormGlobalSMAPE 0.851.

Weights: version 2 of the PyTorch/pytorch-code instance contains the trained weights - the 2-seed phase-A EMA checkpoints (s42/s1337, best val 0.9110/0.9114), per-horizon calibration, normalization stats, and the full code. The model is fine-tunable from these checkpoints.

# References

- AdaptFNO (NeurIPS ML4PS 2025); FourCastNet / AFNO (Pathak et al. 2022); SimVP (Gao et al. CVPR 2022); STL (Cleveland et al. 1990).

instances.usage:
# Model Format

Contains trained weights and code.

Files:
- s42_phaseA_best.pt, s1337_phaseA_best.pt - EMA (eval) weights for the two seeds (AFNOv4, 6.98M params); best val 0.9110 / 0.9114
- horizon_scales.npy - 16 per-horizon multiplicative calibration factors
- stats.npz - per-pixel normalization stats (mean, std, 24h climatology)
- afno_v4.py - full model, data, and inference code
- README.md - load and inference instructions

# Training Data

WRF-Chem simulation over India, 140x124 grid at ~25 km, hourly. Trained on 4 months of 2016 (April, July, October, December). All 20 input channels are derived from the competition data.

# Model Inputs

10 hours of 20-channel gridded fields: observed (9) PM2.5, q2, t2, u10, v10, pblh, psfc, swdown, rain; engineered (5) wind speed, ventilation coefficient, advection, PM tendency, diurnal climatology anomaly; time (2) hour sin/cos; static (4) lat, lon, PM2.5 climatology, episode sigma.

# Model Outputs

16-hour PM2.5 forecast per grid cell, shape (140, 124, 16).

# Model Usage

Load a checkpoint with torch.load(...)['model'] into AFNOv4 (see README.md). Inference averages the two seeds' predictions and applies horizon_scales.

# Fine-tuning

Initialize AFNOv4 from a *_best.pt and continue training. The pipeline in afno_v4.py also supports resume via done-flags and C.PREV.

# Changelog

v2: trained weights (2-seed phase-A EMA) + calibration + stats.
v1: code + stats only (no weights).

# Description

Falcon-H1R Series is a family of reasoning-focused large language models developed by the Technology Innovation Institute (TII) as an extension of the Falcon-H1 architecture. These models are specifically optimized for logical reasoning, mathematical problem solving, coding, planning, and complex instruction following while maintaining high computational efficiency.

Built on the Falcon-H1 hybrid architecture, the models combine Transformer attention with State Space Models (SSMs) to achieve strong reasoning performance, long-context capabilities, and efficient inference. Falcon-H1R models are trained using specialized reasoning datasets and reinforcement learning techniques to improve multi-step reasoning and problem-solving across a wide range of domains.

This collection includes the flagship Falcon-H1R-7B model. By default, this repository is configured to use Falcon-H1R-7B, providing an excellent balance between reasoning capability, coding performance, and inference efficiency for research and production applications.

The model is fully compatible with PyTorch, Hugging Face Transformers, vLLM, and llama.cpp, making it suitable for deployment on Kaggle, local systems, and cloud GPU environments.

License: Falcon-LLM License (TII). Please review the official license terms before using the model in research or commercial applications.

Included Models
| Model                       | Parameters | Purpose            |
| --------------------------- | ---------: | ------------------ |
| **Falcon-H1R-7B (Default)** |         7B | Advanced Reasoning |

**Key Features**
Falcon-H1 Hybrid Architecture
Transformer + State Space Model (SSM)
7B parameter reasoning model
Optimized for mathematical reasoning
Advanced logical reasoning
Strong coding capabilities
Long-context language understanding
Efficient inference
Compatible with PyTorch, Hugging Face Transformers, vLLM, and llama.cpp
Fine-tunable for downstream NLP tasks

## Model Summary

Falcon-H1R-7B is a reasoning-specialized model in the Falcon-H1 family that emphasizes logical reasoning, mathematics, coding, and structured problem solving. Built upon the Falcon-H1 hybrid architecture, it combines Transformer attention with State Space Models to deliver strong reasoning performance while maintaining computational efficiency. The model is well suited for research, AI assistants, code generation, educational applications, and complex reasoning tasks.

## Usage

Falcon-H1R-7B is designed for advanced reasoning, mathematical problem solving, coding, planning, instruction following, AI assistants, research, and downstream NLP applications. The model is fully compatible with PyTorch, Hugging Face Transformers, vLLM, and llama.cpp for deployment across local systems, cloud platforms, and Kaggle notebooks.

# Description

Falcon Edge Series is a family of compact, high-performance language models developed by the Technology Innovation Institute (TII). Built using the BitNet 1.58-bit architecture, these models are designed to deliver strong language understanding, reasoning, and instruction-following capabilities while dramatically reducing memory requirements for deployment on edge devices, mobile platforms, laptops, and resource-constrained environments.

The Falcon Edge family introduces a novel pre-training approach that simultaneously produces both standard and BitNet-compatible model variants, enabling efficient inference and straightforward fine-tuning. Available in 1B and 3B parameter sizes, each model is offered in both Base and Instruct variants to support language modeling, conversational AI, coding, question answering, summarization, and research applications.

By default, this repository is configured to use Falcon-E-1B-Instruct, providing the best balance between inference speed, memory efficiency, and instruction-following performance. Users can switch to any other variant by selecting the appropriate model directory.

The models are fully compatible with PyTorch, Hugging Face Transformers, and BitNet.cpp, making them suitable for deployment on Kaggle, local systems, cloud platforms, and edge devices.

License: Falcon-LLM License (TII). Please review the official license terms before using the models in research or commercial applications.

Included Models
| Model                              | Parameters | Type        |
| ---------------------------------- | ---------: | ----------- |
| **Falcon-E-1B-Instruct (Default)** |         1B | Instruction |
| Falcon-E-1B-Base                   |         1B | Base        |
| Falcon-E-3B-Instruct               |         3B | Instruction |
| Falcon-E-3B-Base                   |         3B | Base        |

**Key Features**
Falcon Edge BitNet 1.58-bit architecture
1B and 3B parameter models
Base and instruction-tuned variants
Ultra-low memory footprint
Optimized for edge AI deployment
Fine-tunable BitNet checkpoints
Compatible with PyTorch, Hugging Face Transformers, and BitNet.cpp
Suitable for Kaggle, local deployment, mobile devices, and embedded AI
Optimized for conversational AI, reasoning, coding, and text generation
Fine-tunable for downstream NLP tasks

## Model Summary

Falcon Edge is a new generation of compact language models that leverages BitNet 1.58-bit technology to significantly reduce memory consumption while maintaining competitive performance. The collection provides efficient models for research, education, conversational AI, coding, and edge deployment. Falcon-E-1B-Instruct is recommended as the default model for general-purpose AI applications, while Falcon-E-3B-Instruct provides improved reasoning and language understanding for more demanding workloads.

## Usage

The Falcon Edge Series is designed for conversational AI, language modeling, reasoning, coding, summarization, question answering, edge AI, mobile deployment, and research. By default, this collection loads Falcon-E-1B-Instruct. To use another model, simply change the model path to the desired variant.

##Disclaimer

***Disclaimer:*** The **Technology Innovation Institute (TII)** and original owners/authors of the model completely reserve the right to contact us regarding the removal of the hosted model.

models.description:
# Description

Falcon-H1-Tiny Series is a collection of extremely compact language models developed by the Technology Innovation Institute (TII) as part of the Falcon-H1 family. These models are designed to deliver impressive language understanding, reasoning, coding, multilingual processing, and tool-calling capabilities while maintaining a tiny memory footprint suitable for edge devices, mobile platforms, embedded systems, and resource-constrained environments.

The Falcon-H1-Tiny family utilizes a hybrid Transformer and State Space Model (SSM/Mamba-inspired) architecture, enabling efficient inference with long-context processing. The collection includes specialized models for general instruction following, multilingual language understanding, Python code generation, function calling, and lightweight reasoning.

By default, this repository is configured to use Falcon-H1-Tiny-90M-Instruct, providing the best balance between speed, memory efficiency, and instruction-following performance. Users can easily switch to other variants depending on their application.

The models are fully compatible with PyTorch and Hugging Face Transformers, making them suitable for deployment on Kaggle, local systems, embedded hardware, Raspberry Pi, and mobile AI applications.

License: Falcon-H1 License (TII). Please review the official license before using the models in research or commercial applications.

Included Models

| Model                                     | Parameters | Purpose            |
| ----------------------------------------- | ---------: | ------------------ |
| Falcon-H1-Tiny-90M-Instruct |        91M | General Chat       |
| **Falcon-H1-Tiny-90M-Base (Default)**                   |        91M | Base Model         |
| Falcon-H1-Tiny-Multilingual-100M-Base     |       100M | Multilingual       |
| Falcon-H1-Tiny-Multilingual-100M-Instruct |       100M | Multilingual Chat  |
| Falcon-H1-Tiny-Coder-90M                  |        91M | Python Coding      |
| Falcon-H1-Tiny-Tool-Calling-90M           |        91M | Function Calling   |
| Falcon-H1-Tiny-R-90M                      |        91M | Reasoning          |
| Falcon-H1-Tiny-R-0.6B                     |       600M | Advanced Reasoning |

**Key Features**
Falcon-H1 Hybrid Architecture
Transformer + State Space (Mamba-inspired) design
Ultra-lightweight models (91M–600M parameters)
Long-context processing (up to 32K tokens for supported models)
General instruction following
Multilingual language understanding
Python code generation
Tool and function calling
Lightweight reasoning models
Optimized for edge AI and embedded deployment
Compatible with PyTorch and Hugging Face Transformers
Fine-tunable for downstream NLP tasks

## Model Summary

The Falcon-H1-Tiny Series demonstrates that highly capable language models can be built with fewer than one billion parameters through specialized training and a hybrid architecture. The collection provides dedicated models for chat, multilingual NLP, reasoning, coding, and tool calling while remaining lightweight enough to run on consumer hardware and edge devices. Falcon-H1-Tiny-90M-Instruct is recommended as the default model for general-purpose conversational AI.

## Usage

The Falcon-H1-Tiny Series is suitable for conversational AI, multilingual applications, Python code generation, function calling, lightweight reasoning, research, education, embedded AI, mobile deployment, and edge computing. The default configuration loads Falcon-H1-Tiny-90M-Instruct. To use another variant, simply update the model path to the desired model directory.

## Disclaimer

***Disclaimer:*** The **Technology Innovation Institute (TII)** and original owners/authors of the model completely reserve the right to contact us regarding the removal of the hosted model.

model of BanglaBERT. Using in this competiton https://www.kaggle.com/competitions/bangla-code-mixed-sentiment-analysis-banglish-benglish

## Usage

**To reload this model in a future notebook** (after adding the saved folder as a Kaggle Dataset input, e.g. `/kaggle/input/models/abdullahshafi2021/banglabert-sentiment-finetuned/pytorch/finetuned-v1/1`):

```python
from transformers import AutoModelForSequenceClassification, AutoTokenizer
import torch

LOAD_DIR = "/kaggle/input/models/abdullahshafi2021/banglabert-sentiment-finetuned/pytorch/finetuned-v1/1"  # adjust to your dataset path

tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(LOAD_DIR)
model = AutoModelForSequenceClassification.from_pretrained("csebuetnlp/banglabert", num_labels=3)
model.load_state_dict(torch.load(f"{LOAD_DIR}/banglabert-model.pth", map_location="cpu"))
model.to(device)
model.eval()
```

requirments -->  pytorch, BanglaBERT

kaggle GPU T4 x 2.
